answer: An operator running 51 keys therefore pays for 51 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. Because the inlet salt is published after the shale checkpoint, the sonnet audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. Answers are salted with a 80 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
